Preston North End v Norwich City (Kick-off 12.30pm). Coverage of the Championship match from Deepdale. Will Keane proved to the be the hero for the Lilywhites when these teams met here last season, as he bagged the equaliser deep into injury-time in what was his first appearance of the season. The Canaries thought they had snatched all three points with five minutes left when Jovon Makama put them 1-0 up, but Keane's return from a long injury spell had the fairytale ending and secured a 1-1 draw.

Ipswich Town v Aston Villa (Kick-off 5.30pm). Coverage of the Premier League match from Portman Road. When these teams faced each other here in a top-flight clash two season ago they shared the spoils in a 2-2 draw that saw the goals scored by players who have since moved on to other clubs, with Liam Delap getting both for the Tractor Boys, while Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins struck for the Villains.

Swansea City v Cardiff City (Kick-off 12.00pm). Coverage of the Championship match from Swansea.com Stadium. The Swans will hope they can continue to rely on their home form in South Wales derby matches, which has seen them win six of the last 10 fixtures in which they served as hosts, while suffering defeat on just two occasions in that same sequence. The most recent clash here was two seasons ago and ended in a 1-1 draw, when Liam Cullen gave the hosts a first-half lead but Callum Robinson equalised for the Bluebirds.

Sunderland v Tottenham Hotspur (Kick-off 2.05pm). Coverage of the top-flight match at Stadium of Light. The corresponding clash last season was the first of Roberto de Zerbi's reign in charge of Spurs, and ended in disappointment when the Black Cats claimed all three points in a 1-0 victory that came courtesy of Nordi Mukiele's heavily deflected strike on goal.

Arsenal v Manchester City (Kick-off 4.30pm). Coverage of the Premier League match from Emirates Stadium. The Gunners laid down a marker for this season with a statement 3-0 win over the Citizens in the Community Shield back in August, and took the lead after just 23 seconds of that contest through Riccardo Calafiori. Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard also got their names on the scoresheet in a totally dominant display for the Premier League champions, as City slipped to defeat in the first match of the post-Pep Guardiola era.

The Patriots claimed a 16-3 victory over the Chargers in an AFC Wild Card game last season at Gillette Stadium, en route to Super Bowl LX, which ultimately ended in defeat and denied them a seventh Championship.

Coverage of the knockout play-off match of the T20 competition, as the third- and fourth-placed teams face each other at a venue to be determined. Perth Scorchers claimed a 28-run victory over Melbourne Stars in the corresponding match last season, scoring 175/5 from their 20 overs before restricting the Stars to 145/9 to secure the win and move on to the Challenger play-off.

South Africa v Bangladesh. Coverage of the first ODI in the three-match series, which takes place at Buffalo Park, East London. The Proteas have historically been the dominant team in one-dayers against the Tigers, winning 19 of the 25 matches played prior to this series, but in more recent times the tourists did claim a memorable 2-1 series victory the last time they came toured South Africa in 2022.

Coventry City v Ipswich Town (Kick-off 8.00pm). Coverage of the top-flight match from Coventry Building Society Arena. The Tractor Boys come into this clash having won the last five meetings against the Sky Blues, four of which were in the Championship and one in the FA Cup. In the games last season they triumphed 3-0 at Portman Road and then came here later the same month to claim a 2-0 victory, with Jack Clarke and Wes Burns getting the goals in the second-half.
